name: acpi_ps_parse_loop
prose: Parses the AML at walk_state->parser_state into a tree of parse ops and returns an ACPICA status. It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER at the start if walk_state->descending_callback is NULL. If ACPI_WALK_METHOD_RESTART is set and the current scope has completed, an IF/WHILE op whose control state is ACPI_CONTROL_PREDICATE_EXECUTING has its predicate evaluated with acpi_ds_get_predicate_value, and the function returns that status when it is a failure that is not an AE_CTRL_* control exception; the scope is then popped (otherwise, if prev_op is set, parsing resumes from prev_op). The main loop runs while parser_state->aml < aml_end or an op is pending. When acpi_ps_create_op fails: under ACPI_PARSE_MODULE_LEVEL AE_ALREADY_EXISTS and AE_NOT_FOUND become AE_OK, AE_CTRL_PARSE_CONTINUE restarts the iteration, AE_CTRL_PARSE_PENDING becomes AE_OK, AE_CTRL_TERMINATE is returned, otherwise acpi_ps_complete_op is called with the status and its failure is returned; if the failed opcode opens a namespace scope, its body is skipped and AE_AML_PACKAGE_LIMIT is returned if the new position lies past aml_end or before the start. If acpi_ps_get_arguments fails, the op is completed with that status (a failure from that call is returned) and, when the control state is an IF or WHILE, the body and a following ELSE are skipped (AE_AML_PACKAGE_LIMIT on out-of-range positions) and the control state is popped and freed. If acpi_ps_push_scope fails the op is completed with that status and a failure from that call is returned. For a finished op it fixes up named.length for region, data-region, create-field and bank-field ops, runs ascending_callback when non-NULL followed by acpi_ps_next_parse_state, turns AE_CTRL_PENDING into AE_OK and, under ACPI_PARSE_MODULE_LEVEL, turns AML-class exceptions, AE_ALREADY_EXISTS and AE_NOT_FOUND into AE_OK, then calls acpi_ps_complete_op and returns its failure if any. When the loop ends it returns the status from acpi_ps_complete_final_op(walk_state, op, status).
note: slice starts mid-function (273-525); read full function psloop.c:221-589. Reviewer R15 claim (only AE_ALREADY_EXISTS/AE_NOT_FOUND downgraded) is wrong for the whole function: psloop.c:559-563 also downgrades ACPI_AML_EXCEPTION(status) from the ascending callback under ACPI_PARSE_MODULE_LEVEL; create_op downgrade at 315-320 is only those two codes. Prior prose wrongly claimed walk_state and the parse tree always remain allocated and owned by caller (acpi_ps_complete_op can pop/delete ops), removed.

name: acpi_ps_complete_final_op
prose: Completes the last parse op and unwinds the remaining parser scopes, returning an ACPICA status. It starts with return_status = status and ascending = TRUE and loops until the scope pop leaves op NULL. For a non-NULL op, while ascending is TRUE and walk_state->ascending_callback is non-NULL, it sets walk_state->op, op_info and opcode, calls the callback and then acpi_ps_next_parse_state. If the resulting status is AE_CTRL_PENDING it calls acpi_ps_complete_op(walk_state, &op, AE_OK) (which can change op) and returns that call's status immediately when it fails, without popping the remaining scopes; when that call succeeds, status has been overwritten by its AE_OK, so the pending status does not propagate. If the status is AE_CTRL_TERMINATE, ascending is cleared and return_status is set to AE_CTRL_TERMINATE; on any other failure ascending is cleared and return_status is overwritten with that status, even if it held an earlier incoming failure. For each non-NULL op, whether or not ascending is still set, acpi_ps_complete_this_op is then called; on failure ascending is cleared and return_status is replaced only if it is currently a success or AE_CTRL_TERMINATE. Each iteration ends by popping a scope into op. The function returns return_status, or the early failure status from acpi_ps_complete_op.
note: Reviewer R15 claim (AE_CTRL_PENDING falls through and becomes the return status after a successful acpi_ps_complete_op) is wrong: psobject.c:666-673 assigns status = acpi_ps_complete_op(..., AE_OK), overwriting AE_CTRL_PENDING with AE_OK. The reviewer's earlier point (early return only on complete_op failure) is right and reflected. Also corrected 'first failure' wording: psobject.c:680-686 overwrites return_status unconditionally for a callback failure.

name: acpi_ps_parse_aml
prose: Runs the AML interpreter loop for a walk state and returns an ACPICA status. It returns AE_BAD_ADDRESS if walk_state->parser_state.aml is NULL. It then creates a thread state; if that fails it calls acpi_ds_terminate_control_method when walk_state->method_desc is set, deletes walk_state with acpi_ds_delete_walk_state and returns AE_NO_MEMORY. Otherwise it records the thread in walk_state, takes the starting sync level from the method when one is executing, pushes the walk state and points acpi_gbl_current_walk_list at the thread. While a current walk state exists it calls acpi_ps_parse_loop only if the status so far is success; frees method_pathname of a nested method; on AE_CTRL_TRANSFER calls acpi_ds_call_control_method (a failure is passed through acpi_ds_method_error) and continues with the new current walk state; converts AE_CTRL_TERMINATE to AE_OK; and for any other non-AE_OK status while executing a method, logs the abort and, for AE_ALREADY_EXISTS on a method not marked serialized, sets ACPI_METHOD_SERIALIZED_PENDING. When a walk state is finished it is popped, its scope stack cleared, the control method terminated (for execute-mode non-module-level walks or when the status is a failure), its parser scope cleaned and the parent method restarted with acpi_ds_restart_control_method using the child's return or implicit return object (a zero integer is created as implicit return in slack mode when there is no return value); on failure the child's return objects are released; for a first-level method the return object (implicit return if present) is stored through caller_return_desc, or released if the caller wants none; finally the finished walk state is deleted. It returns AE_NO_MEMORY immediately, without the final cleanup, if creating that implicit zero integer fails. After the loop it releases all mutexes held by the thread, deletes the thread state, restores acpi_gbl_current_walk_list to its previous value and returns the last status.
note: slice cut the head and is the tail of acpi_ps_parse_aml (psparse.c:422-701); packet name walk_state_execution_loop was not a real function. Fixed under real name. Prior 'dropped' prose omitted AE_BAD_ADDRESS, the AE_NO_MEMORY paths and the status handling.

name: acpi_rs_get_list_length
prose: Walks an AML resource-descriptor byte stream of aml_buffer_length bytes and computes into *size_needed the size of the equivalent internal resource list. *size_needed is first set to ACPI_RS_SIZE_MIN (documented as the minimum size of one end tag). For each descriptor it validates the type and length with acpi_ut_validate_resource and returns that failure status immediately, leaving the partial total in *size_needed. For an END_TAG descriptor it returns AE_OK at once without adding anything for it (the initial ACPI_RS_SIZE_MIN stands in for it). For other descriptors it adds extra bytes that depend on the type (set bits of IRQ/DMA masks, vendor data length minus one, optional resource-source length for address and clock-input descriptors, extra interrupts for extended IRQ, vendor/pin-table lengths for GPIO, pin-function, pin-config and pin-group types, serial-bus sizes), adds the internal structure size plus those extra bytes rounded up to the native word to *size_needed, and advances by the descriptor length. If the buffer is exhausted without an END_TAG it returns AE_AML_NO_RESOURCE_END_TAG.
note: slice cut the head (real function acpi_rs_get_list_length starts rscalc.c:450). Reviewer R15 partly right: END_TAG returns AE_OK at rscalc.c:539-543 before any size is added; but *size_needed is initialised to ACPI_RS_SIZE_MIN (467), so prior wording 'including the END_TAG' was imprecise and is rewritten. Prior prose claimed the function name was acpi_rs_calculate_list_length (wrong name in packet).

name: acpi_rs_get_pci_routing_table_length
prose: Given a Package object that represents a PCI routing table, computes in *buffer_size_needed the size of the corresponding list of routing entries. It reads package_object->package.count elements. For each element it requires a non-NULL Package; a NULL element or one of any other type makes the function return AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE at that point, leaving *buffer_size_needed unmodified. For a valid element it scans the sub-elements until the first one that is a String or a name-class Reference (NULL sub-elements are skipped), adds sizeof(struct acpi_pci_routing_table) - 4, then adds the string length plus one if a String was found, the namespace pathname length of the reference node (acpi_ns_get_pathname_length) if a name Reference was found, or sizeof(u32) if neither was found, and rounds the running total up to a 64-bit boundary. After all elements it stores the total plus sizeof(struct acpi_pci_routing_table) (a terminating entry) in *buffer_size_needed and returns AE_OK. An element count of zero gives just the terminator size.
note: slice cut the head: real function is acpi_rs_get_pci_routing_table_length(package_object, buffer_size_needed) (rscalc.c:733); packet name acpi_calculate_pci_routing_table_length and the prose parameters top_object_list/number_of_elements were wrong (they are locals). Prose rewritten from rscalc.c:733-843.

name: acpi_ut_dump_buffer_to_file
prose: Writes a hex and ASCII dump of count bytes of buffer to the stdio file given as the first parameter, starting the offset column at base_offset. If buffer is NULL it prints the message 'Null Buffer Pointer in DumpBuffer!' and returns. If count is below 4 or odd, display is forced to DB_BYTE_DISPLAY; any display value that is not DB_WORD_DISPLAY, DB_DWORD_DISPLAY or DB_QWORD_DISPLAY is treated as byte display (an invalid display value does not return early). Each output line holds up to 16 bytes: an offset field, the bytes as hex in the chosen unit width (positions past count are filled with spaces), then a space and the ASCII form where isprint() characters are shown as-is and the others as '.'; the final partial line is ended with a newline inside the ASCII loop and the function returns. For word, dword and qword display it reads whole units, so when count is not a multiple of the unit size it can read bytes past count (up to the end of the last unit in the line). Nothing is written when count is zero and buffer is non-NULL. It does not modify buffer and returns no value.
note: slice cut the head (real function acpi_ut_dump_buffer_to_file at utbuffer.c:204; packet name '(unnamed)'). Prior prose wrongly said an invalid display returns immediately with no output (utbuffer.c:243-244 default is byte display) and omitted NULL buffer and count<4/odd forcing byte display (213-220), and its stated precondition did not match the code.

name: acpi_ut_subsystem_shutdown
prose: Shuts down the ACPICA subsystem. If acpi_gbl_shutdown is already set it logs 'ACPI Subsystem is already terminated' and returns without doing anything else (the slice shows only the part after this check). Otherwise it sets acpi_gbl_shutdown to TRUE and clears acpi_gbl_startup_flags; unless ACPI_ASL_COMPILER is defined it calls acpi_ev_terminate and acpi_ut_interface_terminate; it then calls acpi_ns_terminate, acpi_tb_terminate and acpi_ut_terminate, and finally acpi_ut_delete_caches with its status discarded. It returns no value.
note: slice cut the head (real function acpi_ut_subsystem_shutdown, utinit.c:244); the already-shutdown early return at 250-253 was missing from prior prose. Removed unverifiable precondition about in-flight operations.

name: acpi_processor_ffh_lpi_enter
prose: Enters the idle state described by lpi on arm64 through PSCI. It takes the low 32 bits of lpi->address as the PSCI state. If lpi->arch_flags is zero (a retention state) it evaluates CPU_PM_CPU_IDLE_ENTER_RETENTION_PARAM_RCU(psci_cpu_suspend_enter, lpi->index, state), otherwise CPU_PM_CPU_IDLE_ENTER_PARAM_RCU(psci_cpu_suspend_enter, lpi->index, state), and returns the macro's value. In both macros, if lpi->index is zero it calls cpu_do_idle() and returns lpi->index (zero) without calling PSCI. Otherwise, in the non-retention form it first calls cpu_pm_enter(), and if that returns nonzero it skips the suspend and the result is -1; in the retention form cpu_pm_enter() and cpu_pm_exit() are not called. When it proceeds, it calls psci_cpu_suspend_enter(state) (the macros do not call ct_cpuidle_enter/exit because the RCU variant is used), then cpu_pm_exit() in the non-retention form. The result is -1 if psci_cpu_suspend_enter returned nonzero (or cpu_pm_enter failed), otherwise lpi->index. Errno values from cpu_pm_enter or PSCI are not propagated.
note: Checked against include/linux/cpuidle.h:307-350 (__CPU_PM_CPU_IDLE_ENTER). Reviewer R15 partly right: errno values from cpu_pm_enter/PSCI are not returned (macro yields -1 or idx), but cpu_pm_enter is not ignored in the non-retention form (it can make the result -1). Earlier prose was also wrong in other ways: it had retention calling cpu_pm_enter (it is the non-retention form, is_retention=1 skips it), passed two args to psci_cpu_suspend_enter (the macro passes only state), and referred to cpu_cluster_pm_enter, which is not in this macro.

name: BGRT_SHOW(version, version)
prose: Generated function version_show(kobj, attr, buf), a sysfs show callback created by the macro invocation BGRT_SHOW(version, version). It returns sysfs_emit(buf, "%d\n", bgrt_tab.version), i.e. it writes the decimal value of the version member of the global bgrt_tab followed by a newline into buf and returns the number of characters written. sysfs_emit returns zero (after a WARN) instead if buf is NULL or not page-aligned, and the output is limited to PAGE_SIZE; the function does not return a negative error code. kobj and attr are not used. The macro also defines the kobj_attribute bgrt_attr_version.
note: Macro-generated: name is the macro invocation. Checked sysfs_emit (fs/sysfs/file.c:754-768): it returns 0 on bad buf, else vscnprintf length; prior prose claiming a negative error on failure was wrong.

name: acpi_button_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for an ACPI button device. It returns -ENODEV at once, before allocating anything, when the device HID is the lid HID and the module parameter lid_init_state is ACPI_BUTTON_LID_INIT_DISABLED, and -ENOMEM at once if kzalloc of the acpi_button fails (drvdata not yet set in either case). Otherwise it stores the button in pdev drvdata, allocates an input device (failing with -ENOMEM, then freeing the button), and picks the button type by HID (power, sleep or lid, setting the device name, class and, for lid, the input open callback and acpi_lid_notify handler); an unsupported HID logs and sets -ENODEV. If the HID was supported it calls acpi_button_add_fs. If either the HID check or acpi_button_add_fs fails, the input device and the button are freed and that error is returned. It then sets up the input device capabilities and calls input_register_device; on failure it frees the input device, removes the procfs entry, frees the button and returns the error. It then installs a fixed-event handler (device types ACPI_BUS_TYPE_POWER_BUTTON and ACPI_BUS_TYPE_SLEEP_BUTTON) or a notify handler for all notifications; if installation fails it unregisters the input device, removes the procfs entry, frees the button and returns -ENODEV. On success it records the device in lid_device when the button is a lid, calls device_init_wakeup(&pdev->dev, true), logs the name and returns zero. On every failure after platform_set_drvdata the freed button remains stored in pdev's drvdata; the two early returns occur before that point.
note: slice cut the head (real function acpi_button_probe starts button.c:532). Reviewer R15 right: the -ENODEV (lid disabled, 543-545) and -ENOMEM (547-549) returns precede platform_set_drvdata (551), so the prior 'every failure path' wording on drvdata was wrong. Also removed the unverifiable precondition that lid_init_state is already resolved. Error labels: err_input_unregister/err_remove_fs/err_free_button at 662-668.

name: cppc_set_perf
prose: Writes the desired, minimum and maximum performance controls of one CPU's CPPC registers. It returns -ENODEV if the CPU has no cpc_desc. If any of the desired/min/max registers is in PCC space it then requires a valid PCC subspace id for the CPU, returning -ENODEV if it is negative; takes the PCC subspace's pcc_lock for reading; if the platform owns the PCC channel it calls check_pcc_chan(pcc_ss_id, false) and, when that fails, releases the read lock and returns its error. Under the read lock it sets pending_pcc_write_cmd, records pcc_write_cnt in cpc_desc->write_cmd_id and clears write_cmd_status. It then calls cpc_write for the desired register and, only if their values are nonzero, for the min and max registers; the return values of cpc_write are ignored. If any register is in PCC, it releases the read lock and then tries down_write_trylock: on success it sends a PCC write command (send_pcc_cmd, result ignored) if a write is still pending and releases the write lock; otherwise it waits until pcc_write_cnt changes. In the PCC case it returns cpc_desc->write_cmd_status, which send_pcc_cmd sets to the failing result when a write command fails and which is otherwise zero. If no register is in PCC it returns zero after the cpc_write calls. pcc_lock is not held at any return.
note: Read full function cppc_acpi.c:1755-1877. Reviewer R15 wrong: the final return value is cpc_desc->write_cmd_status (1874), and the result of send_pcc_cmd at 1866 is discarded; reviewer R2 (cpc_write errors ignored) is right and reflected.

name: acpi_device_set_power
prose: Sets the ACPI power state of device to state. It returns -EINVAL if device is NULL, device->flags.power_manageable is clear, or state is outside ACPI_STATE_D0..ACPI_STATE_D3_COLD. If state is deeper than D0 and equals device->power.state it returns zero with no change. For a D3cold request the working state becomes D3hot and target_state stays D3cold only if D3cold is marked valid, otherwise D3hot; for other states it returns -ENODEV if device->power.states[state].flags.valid is clear. Unless power.flags.ignore_parent is set, it returns -ENODEV if a parent exists and the working state is shallower (numerically smaller) than the parent's power.state. For a working state deeper than D0 it returns -ENODEV if that state is shallower than device->power.state; evaluates _PSx through acpi_dev_pm_explicit_set only if device->power.state is shallower than D3hot, where failure gives -ENODEV and ends the call without a power-resource transition; then, if the device has power resources, calls acpi_power_transition(device, target_state) and uses its result. For a D0 request it first calls acpi_power_transition(device, D0) when the device has power resources (failure ends the call with that result), then if the current state is already D0 it returns zero without changing anything when _PSC is not available, when evaluating _PSC fails, or when _PSC reports D0; otherwise it evaluates _PS0 via acpi_dev_pm_explicit_set (failure gives -ENODEV). When the transition result is zero, device->power.state is set to target_state and zero is returned; when it is nonzero that value is returned and power.state is left unchanged. The no-change returns also leave power.state unchanged.
note: Read full function device_pm.c:162-293. Reviewer R15 wrong: a failed _PSC evaluation in the D0 case ends in goto no_change (269-270), which returns 0 (289-292), not -ENODEV. Earlier reviewer point (-ENODEV from _PSx failure) is right and present. Note power.state is not updated on the D0 no_change path even though power resources were already turned on.

name: DPTF_POWER_SHOW(name, object)
prose: Macro that defines a sysfs show function name##_show(dev, attr, buf) for each of the DPTF power attributes (for example max_platform_power_mw reading PMAX). The generated function takes the acpi_device from dev_get_drvdata(dev) and calls acpi_evaluate_integer on its handle for the ACPI object whose name is the stringified object argument. If the evaluation succeeds it returns sprintf(buf, "%d\n", (int)val), that is the number of characters written after casting the 64-bit value to int and printing it in decimal with a newline. If it fails it returns -EINVAL without writing to buf. No explicit buffer size limit is applied to the sprintf.
note: Macro-generated; slice lists only a generic name_show; name field is the macro head DPTF_POWER_SHOW(name, object) (dptf_power.c:25-40). Prose matches code (sprintf at 37, -EINVAL at 39).

name: pci_mcfg_lookup
prose: Finds the ECAM configuration-space resource and ops for the PCI root bridge root. If root->mcfg_addr is nonzero (from _CBA) the MCFG list is not searched. Otherwise it walks the whole pci_mcfg_list without stopping at the first match, and for each entry with the same segment whose bus_start is not above root->secondary.start and whose bus_end is not below root->secondary.end it sets root->mcfg_addr to that entry's address, so the last matching entry in list order wins; this stores into root->mcfg_addr even if the function later fails. It then builds a local resource: zeroed, and if root->mcfg_addr is nonzero a memory resource starting at mcfg_addr plus the start bus shifted left by 20 and spanning the bus range size shifted left by 20 bytes. It calls pci_mcfg_apply_quirks, which (with CONFIG_PCI_QUIRKS) may replace the resource start/range and the ops with those of a matching quirk entry; the default ops are pci_generic_ecam_ops. If the resulting resource start is zero it returns -ENXIO leaving *cfgres and *ecam_ops untouched; otherwise it stores the resource in *cfgres and the ops in *ecam_ops and returns zero.
note: slice cut the head (real function pci_mcfg_lookup at pci_mcfg.c:245). Reviewer R15 right: the scan (261-267) has no break so the last match wins, and the test is on bus_res start/end. Prose also now notes root->mcfg_addr is written even on failure.

name: platform_profile_cycle
prose: Advances all registered platform-profile class devices to the next common profile. It takes profile_lock with an interruptible guard and returns -ERESTARTSYS if the lock wait is interrupted (the guard's failure statement is return -ERESTARTSYS), so callers must not already hold profile_lock. Under the lock it aggregates the current profile across handlers with _aggregate_profiles, which reads each handler's profile through get_class_profile and yields that profile if all handlers agree and PLATFORM_PROFILE_CUSTOM if they differ; an error from that scan (a handler's profile_get failing, or -EINVAL for an out-of-range value) is returned. It returns -EINVAL if the aggregate is CUSTOM or still PLATFORM_PROFILE_LAST (no handler registered). It then aggregates the choices (including hidden choices) of all handlers with _aggregate_choices, clears the CUSTOM bit, chooses the next set bit after the current profile with wrap-around, and applies it to each handler with _store_and_notify, which can fail with -EOPNOTSUPP for a handler lacking that choice or with the handler's profile_set error; the first failure is returned and handlers already switched stay switched (each already sent its own class notification), and the legacy platform_profile sysfs notification is not sent. On success it drops the lock, calls sysfs_notify on the legacy platform_profile attribute and returns zero.
note: Read platform_profile.c:334-368, 493-535. Reviewer R15 wrong on both points: scoped_cond_guard(mutex_intr, return -ERESTARTSYS, ...) at 503 returns -ERESTARTSYS itself (not -EINTR), and _aggregate_profiles (334-350) aggregates over all handlers, yielding CUSTOM if they differ, not just the first handler's value. Reviewer R1 (partial switch possible) right and kept.

name: acpi_processor_driver_init
prose: Module init for the ACPI processor driver. If acpi_disabled is set it returns zero without registering anything. Otherwise it calls cpufreq_register_notifier for the policy notifier; if that succeeds it sets acpi_processor_cpufreq_init to true and calls acpi_processor_ignore_ppc_init(), and a failure is not examined. It calls acpi_processor_register_idle_driver() (its result is not checked), then driver_register for acpi_processor_driver; if that returns a negative value the function unregisters the idle driver and, if the cpufreq notifier was registered, unregisters it and clears acpi_processor_cpufreq_init, then returns the negative value without calling driver_unregister. It then calls cpuhp_setup_state(CPUHP_AP_ONLINE_DYN, ..., acpi_soft_cpu_online, NULL); if that returns a negative value it calls driver_unregister, unregisters the idle driver and the cpufreq notifier as above and returns the negative value. On success it stores the returned state in hp_online, registers the CPUHP_ACPI_CPUDRV_DEAD hook with cpuhp_setup_state_nocalls (result ignored), calls acpi_processor_throttling_init, acpi_processor_init_invariance_cppc and acpi_idle_rescan_dead_smt_siblings, and returns zero.
note: Read processor_driver.c:249-302. Reviewer claims across rounds (cpufreq notifier and DEAD hook failures ignored; no driver_unregister on driver_register failure) are right and match the prose. Contract cleared: the old contract (result == 0 || result < 0) is vacuous and the function touches global state.

name: acpi_processor_ffh_lpi_enter
prose: Enters the idle state described by lpi on RISC-V through the SBI HSM suspend call. It takes the low 32 bits of lpi->address as the SBI suspend state. If that state has SBI_HSM_SUSP_NON_RET_BIT set it evaluates CPU_PM_CPU_IDLE_ENTER_PARAM(riscv_sbi_hart_suspend, lpi->index, state), otherwise CPU_PM_CPU_IDLE_ENTER_RETENTION_PARAM(riscv_sbi_hart_suspend, lpi->index, state), and returns the macro's value. In both forms, if lpi->index is zero it calls cpu_do_idle() and returns lpi->index (zero) without suspending. Otherwise the non-retention form first calls cpu_pm_enter() and, if that returns nonzero, skips the suspend and the result is -1; the retention form does not call cpu_pm_enter or cpu_pm_exit. When it proceeds, it calls ct_cpuidle_enter(), riscv_sbi_hart_suspend(state) and ct_cpuidle_exit() (and cpu_pm_exit() in the non-retention form). The result is -1 if riscv_sbi_hart_suspend returned nonzero or cpu_pm_enter failed, otherwise lpi->index; errno values are not propagated.
note: Checked against include/linux/cpuidle.h:307-350 (is_rcu=0 for these macros so ct_cpuidle_enter/exit are called). Reviewer R15 wrong on both points: the macro result is __ret ? -1 : idx (cpuidle.h:331), so success returns lpi->index and failure -1 (not the suspend result), and a nonzero cpu_pm_enter() is not ignored (320-321, it skips the suspend and yields -1). Prior prose said the nonzero suspend value is returned, which is wrong; reviewer R1 (cpu_pm_enter failure path) right.

name: riscv_acpi_update_gsi_range
prose: Searches ext_intc_list in order for the first entry whose gsi_base equals the argument and whose RISCV_ACPI_INTC_FLAG_PENDING flag is set. If one is found it sets that entry's nr_irqs to the nr_irqs argument, clears the pending flag and returns zero. Entries with the same gsi_base but without the pending flag are skipped. If no such entry exists it returns -ENODEV (-19) and the list is unchanged. No allocation is done and the caller gets no reference to a list entry.
note: Read irq.c:75-89. Reviewer R15's complaint was about the formal contract; the contract is cleared since the function reads and writes the global ext_intc_list (rule 4). Prose otherwise matches code; added that non-pending entries with the same gsi_base are skipped.

name: riscv_acpi_register_ext_intc
prose: Allocates a zeroed riscv_ext_intc_list node with kzalloc and returns -ENOMEM (-12) if that fails, leaving ext_intc_list unchanged. Otherwise it records gsi_base, nr_idcs and id in the node (the type argument is not stored). If nr_irqs is nonzero the node's nr_irqs is set to it; if it is zero the node's RISCV_ACPI_INTC_FLAG_PENDING flag is set and nr_irqs is set to U32_MAX - gsi_base. It scans ext_intc_list in order up to the first entry whose gsi_base is lower than the new node's gsi_base (or the end of the list), and inserts the new node just before that point. The entry immediately before the insertion point, if there is one and it has the pending flag set, gets nr_irqs set to the new node's gsi_base minus its own gsi_base (computed in u32). The function then returns zero. The list owns the node afterwards and the caller gets no reference.
note: Read irq.c:134-169. Prose matches code. Contract cleared (touches global list, not a pure integer function); reviewer R15 complaint about the contract is moot. Insertion keeps entries with larger-or-equal gsi_base before the new node, so I describe the insertion point rather than claiming strict ordering.

name: binder_transaction
prose: The function returns no value. At entry it logs, then under the inner proc lock sets thread->ee to BR_OK. It allocates the transaction t (failure: return_error BR_FAILED_REPLY, return_error_param -ENOMEM). For a reply it takes in_reply_to from thread->transaction_stack: an empty stack or a stack whose top is not addressed to this thread gives BR_FAILED_REPLY with -EPROTO, and if the sender thread is gone (binder_get_txn_from_and_acq_inner returns NULL) it gives BR_DEAD_REPLY with return_error_param left at zero; a mismatching sender transaction stack gives BR_FAILED_REPLY/-EPROTO. For a request it resolves the target node through the handle (invalid handle) or the context-manager node; an invalid handle, missing context manager or node-refs failure leaves return_error at BR_FAILED_REPLY, BR_DEAD_REPLY or the code from binder_get_node_refs_for_txn and then sets return_error_param to -EINVAL because no target node was found; a transaction to a context manager owned by the same process or to the sender's own process gives BR_FAILED_REPLY/-EINVAL, a failed security_binder_transaction check gives -EPERM, a synchronous request while the thread's todo head is a transaction work item gives -EPROTO, and a bad transaction stack gives -EPROTO. It allocates tcomplete (-ENOMEM on failure), optionally obtains the sender's security context (error from security_secid_to_secctx, or -EINVAL on extra-size overflow), allocates the target buffer with binder_alloc_new_buf (BR_DEAD_REPLY if -ESRCH else BR_FAILED_REPLY, param = the error), and copies the data and offsets from user space, translating each object by type (binder, handle, fd, fd array, buffer/pointer; other types give -EINVAL; copy faults -EFAULT; translation errors propagate). Then it queues: for a reply, the transaction to the target thread and tcomplete to the sender thread; for a synchronous request, tcomplete is queued deferred, t is pushed on the sender's transaction stack and binder_proc_transaction is called; for a oneway request binder_proc_transaction is called without a thread, and tcomplete is queued (type BINDER_WORK_TRANSACTION_PENDING if the target is frozen and the transaction was queued pending); a failure there (or a dead target thread) goes to the error exit. On success it drops the temporary references (target_thread, target_proc, target_node) and returns. On any failure it dequeues tcomplete if queued, frees tcomplete, releases the target buffer if one was allocated, drops the target node references, frees t, drops temporary references on target_thread and target_proc, records return_error, return_error_param and return_error_line in the transaction logs and, for a reply failure with in_reply_to set, sets the sender's error and calls binder_send_failed_reply on in_reply_to and queues BR_TRANSACTION_COMPLETE to the calling thread; otherwise it records the extended error on thread->ee and queues return_error as thread->return_error work.
note: Read full function binder.c:3073-3935. Slice covers t allocation, reply/request target resolution, tcomplete allocation and security context. Reviewers R1/R2/R15 right: BR_FAILED_REPLY/BR_DEAD_REPLY on invalid handle (3224-3227), no context manager (3237) and node-refs failure set return_error only there, but the !target_node exit (3248-3254) then sets return_error_param=-EINVAL; the empty reply stack sets -EPROTO (3155); the reply-target-gone path (3184-3186) leaves param 0. Prior prose also said return_error is left 0 on success, but a oneway send to a frozen process leaves BR_TRANSACTION_PENDING_FROZEN there (3813-3827), and it omitted the extra-size overflow path.

name: ata_eh_reset
prose: Performs the reset sequence for link and returns zero or a negative errno. First it sets max_tries to the number of entries in ata_eh_reset_timeouts (1 if ATA_LFLAG_RST_ONCE) and drops hardreset or softreset if the link flags forbid them. If a reset was done earlier it sleeps until ATA_EH_RESET_COOL_DOWN after ehc->last_reset. It sets ATA_PFLAG_RESETTING under ap->lock, calls ata_eh_about_to_do, resets each device's PIO/DMA mode state, clears ATA_EH_RESET from ehc->i.action and sets ATA_EH_HARDRESET if a hardreset exists, else ATA_EH_SOFTRESET if a softreset exists. If prereset exists it runs it (and on the slave link too, when the first result is zero or -ENOENT); a nonzero result is handled as follows: -ENOENT clears ATA_EH_RESET, sets all the link's device classes to ATA_DEV_NONE and the function returns zero without thawing the port; any other nonzero value is returned as the error. If a reset method exists and prereset cleared ATA_EH_RESET, classes are set to ATA_DEV_NONE, a frozen host port is thawed and zero is returned. Otherwise it loops: for a host link it freezes the port, runs the reset (and a slave-link hardreset and, when ata_eh_followup_srst_needed says so, a follow-up softreset; a missing softreset gives -EINVAL); failures other than -EAGAIN from the first reset, a failed slave reset or a failed follow-up reset go to the failure handling. With no reset method it skips the reset and assumes ATA class unless ATA_LFLAG_ASSUME_CLASS is set. After a reset it updates device state and classes for devices whose physical link is not offline, records link speeds when SCR status can be read, thaws a host port, calls postreset, clears cached SError, and cross-checks link online state against classes; if classify is set, devices are misclassified and tries remain, it fails with -EAGAIN to retry. On success it calls ata_eh_done for the link (and slave), sets ehc->last_reset, sets ATA_EH_REVALIDATE, sets link->lpm_policy to ATA_LPM_UNKNOWN and returns zero. Failure handling: for a non-host link whose SCR status cannot be read the status becomes -ERESTART; when tries are exhausted it thaws a host port, logs and returns the last status; otherwise it waits out the remaining time to the deadline (releasing EH ownership while waiting), then if the status is -ERESTART thaws a host port and returns it, else lowers the speed limit (of both links on the last try, of the failed link on -EPIPE) and retries. All exits clear ATA_EHI_HOTPLUGGED on the link and slave and ATA_PFLAG_RESETTING under ap->lock before returning.
note: slice cut the head (real function ata_eh_reset at libata-eh.c:2815). Reviewer R15 right: the prereset -ENOENT exit (2923-2935) does not thaw the port; only the 'prereset cleared ATA_EH_RESET' exit (2941-2947) thaws. Prior prose also omitted that other prereset errors are returned directly and some control flow detail. Single return at 3157 so cleanup at out: runs for all exits.

name: ata_eh_revalidate_and_attach
prose: Revalidates enabled devices of link and probes and configures new ones. It walks the devices in reverse order. For an enabled device with ATA_EH_REVALIDATE pending it first sets the link to ATA_LPM_MAX_POWER via ata_eh_link_set_lpm if lpm_policy is above that (failure aborts), returns -EIO if the device's physical link is not established, marks the revalidate action begun, calls ata_dev_revalidate (failure aborts), marks it done, sets ATA_EHI_SETMODE and schedules ap->scsi_rescan_task. For a device whose class is ATA_DEV_UNKNOWN, with tries left and an enabled class in ehc->classes, it temporarily sets dev->class and either calls sata_pmp_attach (PMP class) or ata_dev_read_id, stores the resulting class back in ehc->classes and resets dev->class to unknown; on success it clears the device's error ring and adds it to a new-device mask, on -ENOENT it thaws the port and leaves the device ignored (the function can still return zero), and any other error aborts. After the loop, if a reset was done on a host link it calls the port's cable_detect hook (if any) and ata_force_cbl. It then configures each new non-PMP device in forward order: it sets ATA_EHI_PRINTINFO around ata_dev_configure, on failure sets the device class back to unknown and aborts, and otherwise sets ATA_PFLAG_SCSI_HOTPLUG under ap->lock and ATA_EHI_SETMODE. It returns zero when it completes. On abort it clears ATA_DFLAG_RESUMING on the failing device, stores that device in *r_failed_dev and returns the error, which is the negative errno from ata_eh_link_set_lpm, ata_dev_revalidate, sata_pmp_attach, ata_dev_read_id or ata_dev_configure, or -EIO for the link-not-established check.
note: slice is mostly the tail of ata_eh_reset plus helpers; real function ata_eh_revalidate_and_attach at libata-eh.c:3289-3431 was read in full. Reviewer R2 (omits ata_set_mode returns) is wrong: ata_set_mode is not called in this function. Reviewer R15 (-EHOSTDOWN) is not shown by this function's code; errors from ata_dev_configure are covered generically. The -ENOENT case is correct (3377-3383, ends with return 0 at 3425).

name: ata_bitfield_name_search(class, ata_class_names)
prose: Generated function get_ata_class_names(table_key, buf), created by the macro invocation ata_bitfield_name_search(class, ata_class_names). It scans ata_class_names in order for the first entry whose value equals table_key, writes that entry's name into buf with sprintf and stops scanning; it then writes a newline with sprintf and returns the total number of characters written. If no entry matches only the newline is written and the result is 1, so the result is at least 1. No buffer size is checked: buf must hold the longest name ("unknown", 7 characters), the newline and the terminating NUL.
note: Macro-generated (libata-transport.c:109-125, table at 130-143). Reviewer R15 right: the table contains "unknown" (7 chars), so the earlier 5-character bound was wrong.

name: sis_133_mode_filter
prose: ATA mode_filter callback that removes the UDMA6 and UDMA7 transfer modes when ATA133 is not enabled. It computes port = sis_port_base(adev) (a PCI configuration offset that is 0x40 or 0x70 depending on bit 30 of the dword at 0x54, plus 8 per port number and 4 per device number), reads the 32-bit PCI configuration dword at that offset from the host's PCI device into t1 without checking the read's return value, and if bit 0x08 of t1 is clear returns mask with the bits (0xC0 << ATA_SHIFT_UDMA) cleared, which with ATA_SHIFT_UDMA = 12 is 0xC0000 (the UDMA6 and UDMA7 bits); if bit 0x08 is set it returns mask unchanged. It does not modify any state besides its local variables.
note: Checked include/linux/libata.h:319-325: ATA_SHIFT_PIO=0, ATA_SHIFT_MWDMA=7, ATA_SHIFT_UDMA=12, so 0xC0<<12 = 0xC0000. All reviewer claims (R1/R2/R15: 0xC000, 0x3000 or ATA_SHIFT_UDMA=0) are wrong, as was the old prose (0x3000). Removed the claim that a failed read yields all ones (return value is unchecked).

name: he_start
prose: Initializes the ForeRunnerHE adapter hardware for the atm_dev and returns zero on success or a negative errno; it does not release resources itself on its error returns. It reads PCI config and the BAR 0 address and sets GEN_CNTL_0 flags; returns -EINVAL if reading or writing GEN_CNTL_0 fails, if reading or writing PCI_COMMAND fails, if reading PCI_CACHE_LINE_SIZE or PCI_LATENCY_TIMER fails, if ioremap of HE_REGMAP_SIZE bytes fails, or if the reset status bit BOARD_RST_STATUS is not set after reset. Failures when writing the cache line size or latency timer are only logged. It then sets bus width, reads the PROM, programs byte swapping and the SDRAM controller, and calls he_init_irq, returning its nonzero error if it fails. It returns -ENODEV if both nvpibits and nvcibits are given and their sum is not HE_MAXCIDBITS. It programs the buffer map and hardware registers, clears connection memory, initializes buffer pools, the CS block (returning -ENOMEM if he_init_cs_block_rcm fails) and the TPD ring, creates the tpd dma pool (-ENOMEM on failure), sets up group 0 with he_init_group (-ENOMEM if it fails), clears the other groups, allocates the host status page (-ENOMEM on failure), initializes the framer when configured, enables transmit and receive, resets the stper table and peaks and sets the atm_dev ci_range from vpibits/vcibits; then it returns zero. On its error returns this function performs no cleanup of its own: the ioremap mapping stored in he_dev->membase and any IRQ, pool or buffer set up before the failure are not released here.
note: Read he.c:970-1521 (slice is mid-function). Reviewer R15 right: cache-line and latency-timer writes only log (1023-1024, 1044-1045); reads fail with -EINVAL (1016-1018, 1027-1029). Prior prose also listed the board reset check and ioremap as -EINVAL (correct) and claimed the caller must iounmap membase (unverifiable from this function; replaced with a statement that he_start does no cleanup itself).

name: he_open
prose: Opens an ATM VCC on the HE adapter. It returns zero immediately, touching nothing, when vci is ATM_VCI_UNSPEC or vpi is ATM_VPI_UNSPEC. Otherwise it sets ATM_VF_ADDR and allocates an he_vcc with kmalloc(GFP_ATOMIC); if that fails it returns -ENOMEM with ATM_VF_ADDR still set and vcc->dev_data unchanged. It stores the he_vcc in vcc->dev_data. If the transmit traffic class is not ATM_NONE it computes a PCR goal, returns -EINVAL for an AAL other than AAL5 or AAL0 or for a traffic class other than UBR or CBR, returns -EBUSY if the connection's TSR0 state is nonzero, and for CBR returns -EBUSY if the total bandwidth would exceed 90 percent of the link rate or no cs_stper register is free (otherwise it reserves one, adding to total_bw and cs_stper inuse), then programs the TSR registers. If the receive traffic class is not ATM_NONE it returns -EINVAL for an AAL other than AAL5 or AAL0, returns -EBUSY if RSR0 shows the connection already open, and otherwise programs the RSR registers and opens the connection. On any error the he_vcc is freed with kfree and ATM_VF_ADDR is cleared, but vcc->dev_data is not reset and any transmit-side registers or CBR reservation already made before a later receive-side failure are not undone. On success it sets ATM_VF_READY and returns zero.
note: slice cut the head (real function he_open at he.c:2116-2326). Reviewer R15 wrong: set_bit(ATM_VF_ADDR) happens at 2131, before the kmalloc at 2135, so the kmalloc failure returns -ENOMEM with ATM_VF_ADDR still set; the old prose was right on that. Added: dev_data left dangling after kfree, and tx state not undone on rx failure.

name: dequeue_rx
prose: Handles one entry of the receive status queue. It reads the STAT register to refresh card->sbfqc and card->lbfqc, removes the skb for rsqe->buffer_handle from card->idr and returns without further action if none is found; otherwise it syncs and unmaps the DMA buffer. If the vpi or vci is out of range, or the virtual circuit does not have receive set, it recycles the buffer and returns. For an AAL0 circuit it allocates a small skb per cell; on allocation failure it adds the remaining cell count to rx_drop and stops; if atm_charge fails it frees that skb, adds the remaining count minus one to rx_drop and stops; otherwise it builds a 4-byte header, copies the 48-byte cell, pushes it to the vcc and increments rx. It then recycles the original buffer and returns. For AAL5 it takes the circuit's iovec buffer (or dequeues or allocates one, dropping the cell with rx_drop and recycling the buffer if allocation fails), appends the skb as an iovec entry (resetting the iovec list with rx_err if it already holds NS_MAX_IOVECS entries), and returns unless this is the end of the PDU. At the end of the PDU it reads the AAL5 trailer length; on a CRC error or a length mismatch it increments rx_err, recycles all buffers and the iovec buffer and returns. Otherwise it delivers the SDU: a single small buffer, a small plus large buffer (using the small one if the length fits NS_SMBUFSIZE, else copying the small buffer into the large one), or a huge buffer assembled from the pieces; atm_charge or huge buffer allocation failures increment rx_drop and recycle the buffers instead of delivering, and delivered SDUs increment rx. Finally it clears vc->rx_iov and recycles the iovec buffer. It returns no value.
note: slice is the tail of dequeue_rx (nicstar.c:1975-2331); packet name ns_process_rsqe is not a function in this file. Fixed under the real name rather than dropped. Prior prose was too vague (one-line summary) and omitted the AAL0 path and error counters.

name: valid_zones_show
prose: Sysfs show callback (compiled only with CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE) for a memory block's valid_zones attribute; it returns the number of characters written to buf. If mem->state is MEM_ONLINE it writes the name of mem->zone followed by a newline, or "none" followed by a newline if mem->zone is NULL (the block spans multiple zones). In any other state it computes the default zone for the block's pfn range with zone_for_pfn_range(MMOP_ONLINE, ...), writes its name, then appends a space and a zone name for the kernel online type and one for the movable online type, each only when that zone differs from the default zone, and ends with a newline.

Prior prose said 'the allowed kernel and movable zone lists' unconditionally; print_allowed_zone returns nothing when the zone equals the default (481-482), corrected.

name: CACHE_ATTR(size, "%llu")
prose: Generated function size_show(dev, attr, buf), created by CACHE_ATTR(size, %llu). It returns sysfs_emit(buf, "%llu\n", to_cache_info(dev)->cache_attrs.size), that is it formats the size member of the node cache attributes of the node_cache_info containing dev with the format %llu and a newline, and returns the number of characters written. sysfs_emit truncates to PAGE_SIZE and returns zero (after a warning) if buf is NULL or not page-aligned; it does not return a negative error. note: Macro-generated (node.c:302-316). Reviewer R15 right: sysfs_emit (fs/sysfs/file.c:754-768) truncates via vscnprintf and returns 0 on bad buf, never negative; prior prose claiming a negative error was wrong.
